name: Trap Bar Heavy Farmer's Carry
description: The trap bar farmer's carry uses a hexagonal trap bar as the carrying implement, loading very heavy weights while keeping the load centred at the body's midline rather than hanging at the sides. The trap bar's neutral-grip handles and frame allow heavier loads than standard farmer's handles for most athletes, while the centred load distribution reduces spinal lateral flexion demands and allows trainees to overload the grip and trapezius safely. It is a staple in strength and conditioning programmes for developing absolute carry strength and grip endurance.

execution.starting_position: The trap bar is on the floor. Step inside the frame, feet hip-width apart. Grip the high handles. Hinge at the hips to reach the handles, back flat.
execution.setup_instructions: Use the high handles for most carry work — they reduce the range of motion of the initial deadlift and allow heavier loading. Ensure plates are secured with collars before walking.
steps: Step 1: Deadlift the trap bar from the floor: hinge, brace, stand up with hips and knees extending simultaneously.
Step 2: Once standing, adjust posture — tall, shoulders back, core braced firmly.
Step 3: Walk with short, quick steps. Keep the frame of the bar travelling straight — do not let it swing or sway forward.
Step 4: Maintain upright posture throughout the walk. Keep the gaze forward.
Step 5: At the end of the distance, reduce pace and lower the bar by hinging at the hips.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe short and regularly throughout the carry. Full brace before the initial lift from the floor.
common_mistakes: Letting the bar drift forward or backward during the walk, causing the trap bar frame to contact the legs
Overstriding, which creates instability and reduces walking speed
safety_considerations: Ensure collars are tight before carrying — a shifting plate inside the trap bar frame is a serious hazard
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Walk 20–40 metres per set at heavy loads. At moderate loads, 40–60 metres.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Strength: 20–30m at 1.5–2× bodyweight × 4–5 sets. Rest 2–3 minutes. Conditioning: 40m at bodyweight × 5–6 sets with 60–90 seconds rest.
coaching_cues: Crush the handles — do not relax the grip
